newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude prices drift ahead of Christmas holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude prices drift ahead of Christmas holiday.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices drifted ahead of the Christmas holiday Tuesday morning as most traders had already departed for the two-day celebration.
February West Texas Intermediate hovered around $24.80-90 a barrel, up 20 cents from late Monday due to technical factors. March WTI was pegged at $24.10-20 a barrel.
"It's very dead out there, most people are already out," one trader said.
The NYMEX closes early today at 1300 EST/1800 GMT to observe Christmas. ACCESS electronic trading will resume December 25 at 1900 EST/0000 GMT.
February grade business was subdued, with no deals reported. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was pegged around WTI/Cushing plus 45-50 cents a barrel, up two to three cents from late Monday.
WTI/Midland was valued at flat to two cents premium, while Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was around 50 cents premium.
The recent opening of the trans-Atlantic arbitrage has put pressure on domestic sweet grades.
Sour grades, in contrast, have picked up on brighter fundamentals. West Texas Sour/Midland was around WTI/Cushing minus $1.40-1.50 a barrel.
Lightly traded Eugene Island was stuck in a wide range at minus $1.20-80 a barrel.
The completion of hydrostatic testing on Canadian pipelines and production snags on a Mobil platform in the Gulf of Mexico have improved the sour supply balance.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was talked at $2.42-50 a barrel. The Feb/Mar WTI spread was around 67 cents.
